title: Why do you feel lonely even around people?

lines.speaker: miko
lines.text: Being included doesn't always mean feeling understood.

lines.speaker: miko
lines.text: Loneliness is the gap between the connection you want and the connection you feel.

lines.speaker: miko
lines.text: More people won't always close that gap.

lines.speaker: miko
lines.text: Sometimes you laugh, say you're fine, and go home feeling invisible.

lines.speaker: miko
lines.text: One place to start is an honest answer to someone you trust.

lines.speaker: miko
lines.text: Honestly? It's been a rough week.

lines.speaker: mia
lines.text: Same. I only came for the snacks.

lines.speaker: miko
lines.text: First real conversation of the night.

visualStory: Open with WHY / DO / YOU / FEEL / ALONE, one word at a time, synchronized with the spoken question.
On ALONE, shift to black-gray-blue, shake the word once, and surround sad Miko with person icons. Carry the composition smoothly into the explainer.
Keep his blue I'm fine message as the shared object. Morph the crowd UI into a conversation diagram.
The message stretches into two avatar endpoints with a visible gap. Extra contacts arrive without bridging it.
The diagram folds back into the same I'm fine reply, with Miko looking down at his phone.
The crowd gives way to one friend's chat. A You okay? message arrives.
The blue reply changes to It's been a rough week and travels to the friend when sent.
The green reply arrives. Reveal Mia holding a sandwich for the snack joke, then hold both characters' relief.

Enlarge the connection graphic and keep blue bars and sparkles behind opaque portrait cards. On the second connection phrase, sweep a cyan-white shimmer along the separated bars while preserving the visible gap.
factualBoundaries: Loneliness concerns perceived missing connection, not a headcount alone.
The party, dialogue and outcome are fictional examples.
An honest exchange is offered as a possible place to start, not a guaranteed cure or the only cause of loneliness.
Do not introduce unsupported brain scans, hormones, statistics or diagnostic claims.
